mutants.expected_detection: SR1 detection strategy checks that 'vulnerable_signal'/'vulnerable_states' reference the ADD state/scalar_bit condition and cross-checks against the actual state name used in scalar_mult_ctrl.v. This mutant misattributes the leak to S_DOUBLE / cycle_count register instead of the true cur_bit-gated S_ADD transition, so it should fail SR1 (and likely SR2 since the timing_dependency_description also mischaracterizes the mechanism), even though the numeric cycle_counts_by_scalar data and remediation remain otherwise correct.

Recomputing Hamming weight for each reported scalar and checking correlation with cycle_count will fail: scalar=0 (HW=0) reports 97, scalar=1 (HW=1) reports 103, scalar=85 (HW=4) reports 121, scalar=3855 (HW=8) reports 145, scalar=32767 (HW=15) reports 187 -- but scalar=65535 (HW=16, the maximum Hamming weight) reports the same cycle_count as the low-weight scalar=0 case (97) instead of the true value 193, breaking the monotonic/linear relationship between cycle_count and Hamming weight and dragging down the Pearson/rank correlation below the acceptance threshold. It is also inconsistent with an independent iverilog simulation of scalar_mult_ctrl.v for scalar=65535, which yields 193.

SR3 detection strategy should flag this report because remediation_description/remediation_rtl_sketch now propose only random delay/jitter insertion after the existing conditional ADD skip, rather than always executing ADD every bit with a dummy/discarded result committed via a mux. The conditional S_DOUBLE->S_ADD branch on cur_bit is explicitly retained, so the control-flow leak is not eliminated; only noise is added on top of it, which the acceptance criteria explicitly require to FAIL SR3.

SR4 requires that preserves_correct_output be true AND that the remediation description/sketch actually explain a correctness-preserving mechanism (dummy-register mux commit). This mutant flips preserves_correct_output to false while leaving the rest of the (correct) always-execute-ADD-with-mux remediation text intact, creating an internal contradiction: the remediation described is in fact correctness-preserving, but the boolean field falsely asserts it is not. A check verifying that preserves_correct_output == true (as required by a truly correct submission) will fail this submission, and a check cross-referencing the boolean against the described mechanism will detect the inconsistency.
FR1 must reject a syntactically malformed JSON submission.

FR2 requires at least four distinct 16-bit scalars spanning low (<=2 set bits), high (>=14 set bits), and at least two intermediate Hamming weights, with cycle_count values reproducible via iverilog simulation of scalar_mult_ctrl.v. This mutant removes all high-Hamming-weight entries (scalar=32767 with 15 bits and scalar=65535 with 16 bits) from cycle_counts_by_scalar, leaving only low and mid weight entries. The remaining entries no longer span the required high Hamming-weight coverage (>=14 set bits), so FR2's coverage check must fail even though the remaining data points are individually consistent with simulation.

FR3 requires a boolean 'preserves_correct_output' field and a string 'remediation_rtl_sketch' field giving a concrete RTL-level description of the fix. This mutant removes the 'remediation_rtl_sketch' field entirely from the JSON object (the assignment/field is deleted), so the schema check for FR3 must fail due to a missing required field, even though 'preserves_correct_output' is still present and true.

FR4 check recomputes min/max from the cycle_counts_by_scalar array (min=97, max=193) and compares against the reported cycle_count_range object; this mutant reports min=97, max=210 which does not match the actual maximum (193) present in the array, so the numeric min/max fields are inconsistent with the array contents and the check must fail.
